facts.fact_text: Despite the position of the district authority, the organisers decided to hold a public gathering in Tverskaya Square on 27 November 2005 at 2 p.m.
The special security squad proceeded to arrest some participants at the public gathering in Tverskaya Square on 27 November 2005.
The special security squad allegedly did not give participants time or opportunity to disperse after a verbal order to do so before making arrests.
The applicants, along with fifty other people, were taken to the Tverskoy police station following the public gathering on 27 November 2005.

Under sections 5 and 7 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act in force at the relevant time, the organiser of a public event (except for an event involving one person) was required to inform the competent authority of the event at least ten days in advance.

Under sections 5 and 7 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act in force at the relevant time, the organiser of a picket (пикетирование) was required to inform the competent authority at least three days in advance.

Under sections 5 and 7 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, the organiser was required to indicate the purpose of the event, its form, the venue and the itinerary, as well as the date, timing and approximate number of participants.
Under the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, the competent authority was required to notify the organiser if it had a reasoned proposal for another venue and/or timing for the event.
Under the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, the organiser was required to inform the competent authority whether he or she refused or accepted the suggested new venue and/or timing.
Under section 5 § 5 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, the event could not take place if the event organiser and the competent authority had not approved the alternative proposal.
The district authority's letter of 24 November 2005 referred to the 'security of the participants' as a reason for the suggested change of venue and timing.
The district authority's letter of 24 November 2005 referred to the need to avoid causing obstruction to pedestrians and vehicles as a reason for the suggested change of venue and timing.
